selectedOptionText: Reject the candidate until it meets the critical-field floor and full-route target.
controllingFact: A hard 2% critical-field ceiling is breached at 4.7%; latency gain cannot compensate for violating a release constraint.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Accept because p95 improved by 30% and the quality regression is small in absolute terms.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A faster route is a credible benefit, but 4.7% exceeds the explicit ceiling, so the release is ineligible.

selectedOptionText: Compare end-to-end outcomes on all assigned requests, treating timeouts and missing completions explicitly alongside latency among completed requests.
controllingFact: The denominator must include assigned requests and separately expose timeouts/missing completions; completed-only p95 is survivor-biased.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Compare p95 only among completed requests for both versions.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Completed-only latency is useful as one metric, but cannot establish service speed if timeout rates differ.

selectedOptionText: Parallelize independent lookups, then verify after all required results arrive.
controllingFact: The four lookups are independent; the verifier depends on all four and therefore must remain after their join.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Parallelize the verifier with the lookups so the response starts earlier.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Parallelizing verification before its evidence exists violates the dependency and can produce premature output.

selectedOptionText: Honor retry-after with a bounded retry policy and compare full-route outcomes.
controllingFact: A transient 429 has a documented retry-after; bounded retries should honor it and measure full-route latency/recovery.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Retry every error once after the same fixed delay, including validation and authorization errors.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A fixed retry for all errors includes permanent validation/auth failures and ignores provider guidance.

selectedOptionText: Use the approved async path and preserve final validation as the completion contract.
controllingFact: The consumer allows either a complete ≤1s response or an approved async acknowledgment followed by later validated completion.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Stream provisional output and assume it counts as the one-second completed response.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Provisional streaming is not the required completed result and does not meet the stated completion contract.

selectedOptionText: Add service-supported idempotency or reconciliation before retrying unknown writes.
controllingFact: A lost response leaves a non-idempotent write outcome unknown; retry safety requires service idempotency or reconciliation.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Retry only when the client receives no response within 500 ms.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A short timeout does not tell whether the write committed, so retrying can duplicate it.

selectedOptionText: Compare resolution quality, completion, 429 recovery, tail latency, and cost on a representative workload, then expand only if the full contract remains satisfied.
controllingFact: Rollout must test quality, completion, throttling/recovery, tail latency, and cost on representative traffic; median alone is insufficient.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Roll out because the median improved and the p95 target still passes.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: The p95 target passing is necessary but says nothing about quality, completion, or elevated 429 recovery.

selectedOptionText: Correlate provider completion, gateway delivery, browser receipt, and durable commit as separate events for the same logical operation and attempt.
controllingFact: The missing boundary lies between provider completion, delivery/receipt, and durable commit; events need shared logical-operation and attempt linkage.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Record only model completion latency because the provider reports success.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Provider success alone does not show that the browser received or the database committed the answer.

selectedOptionText: Link worker and parent attempts with task, source, and merge identifiers.
controllingFact: Parent retries can overlap workers; task/source/merge identifiers link each worker result to its parent attempt and synthesis.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Give every worker the parent’s single request ID and omit worker identifiers.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A shared request ID alone collapses distinct worker and retry attempts, preventing ownership attribution.

selectedOptionText: Keep a representative baseline sample and add a bounded event rule for denials with policy decision, operation, latency, and safe identifiers.
controllingFact: Rare denials need an outcome-triggered bounded sample with safe dimensions while baseline sampling remains representative.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Count denial events only and discard route, decision, and timing dimensions.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Counting denials without route/decision/timing data cannot estimate the requested rate and latency distribution.

controllingFact: No option resolves operation state across attempts. The decisive facts are that attempt one committed and attempt two was a duplicate denial; record per-attempt outcomes and derive operation success from the durable commit.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Mark the final attempt’s denial as the operation result and discard earlier attempts.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Treating the last duplicate denial as the whole operation result is the closest offered alternative, but discards the earlier committed effect and mislabels success.

selectedOptionText: Keep routine traces metadata-only and implement narrowly scoped, time-bounded, audited access to the approved redacted incident excerpt.
controllingFact: Routine telemetry should be metadata-only; access to a redacted incident excerpt must be scoped, time-bounded, and audited.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Retain all full prompts but encrypt the log bucket.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Encryption does not justify retaining all full prompts or narrow the operator’s access.

controllingFact: Useful attribution requires separate prompt and retriever version identifiers on the same request/outcome; causal links and clock handling alone do not identify which component changed.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Add a free-form operator note naming whichever component seems responsible.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A free-form guess is the nearest offered attribution aid, but it is not reproducible evidence and adds no component version.

selectedOptionText: Carry trace context through enqueue and worker execution, with timestamps for enqueue, dequeue, attempts, tool/model stages, and completion.
controllingFact: Trace context and stage timestamps across enqueue/dequeue, retries, model/tools, and completion separate queue delay from execution.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Measure only total wall-clock time from the browser.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Browser wall time supplies only the total and cannot distinguish queue wait from downstream stages.

selectedOptionText: Whether the stream reached its terminal completion event and whether the application assembled and delivered the expected final payload.
controllingFact: Transport/HTTP success and received deltas do not prove terminal stream completion or assembled final payload delivery.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Use HTTP 200 as the completion signal for the whole answer.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: HTTP 200 is only transport status, not proof of completed application output.

selectedOptionText: Define completion at durable result commit, distinct from queue acknowledgment.
controllingFact: A queue acknowledgment can precede persistence; completion must be anchored to durable result commit.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Queue acknowledgment, because it proves the worker received the task.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Acknowledgment proves receipt/handling, not durable successful work.

selectedOptionText: Link synthesis spans to the worker results and evidence they consumed.
controllingFact: The lead’s final claim needs provenance links to worker outputs and evidence consumed, beyond a shared user or trace.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: A single free-text note written after the final answer.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A free-text summary cannot reliably map a claim to the source worker evidence.

selectedOptionText: Add queue, retrieval, tool, model, validation, and delivery spans.
controllingFact: Without queue/retrieval/tool/validation/delivery spans, subtracting model time leaves an unlabeled mixture; instrument material stages.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Subtract model duration from overall duration and label the remainder as queue time.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: The residual includes all non-model stages, not just queue time.

selectedOptionText: Use trace links for causality and clock metadata for cross-service timestamps.
controllingFact: Causal trace links preserve happens-before relationships despite skew; clock metadata explains imperfect cross-service wall times.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Sort events by local wall-clock timestamp and increase the viewer’s allowed skew window.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Sorting by local timestamps preserves the skew-induced impossible order.

selectedOptionText: Segment by source structure, preserve prerequisites, and test both query classes.
controllingFact: Structure-aware segmentation can keep short checklist units precise and preserve long procedure prerequisites; evaluate both query classes.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Keep the fixed chunking and increase top-k until both content types appear.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Larger global chunks may reduce short-step precision and do not test both content classes.

selectedOptionText: Keep each prerequisite with its dependent step, or retrieve an explicit link with it.
controllingFact: Step 4’s applicability condition is part of its meaning; preserve the prerequisite link with the dependent step.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Increase overlap uniformly by 50 tokens across all chunks.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Uniform overlap may omit the conditional relation and cannot guarantee the condition accompanies step 4.

selectedOptionText: Index each table value with its column label and row identity.
controllingFact: Table values are ambiguous without headers and row identity; index them together.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Add the table title to every row and leave the columns out.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A title alone does not distinguish effective date, notice period, and renewal rule.

selectedOptionText: Compare language-specific and aligned retrieval using paired revision-aware queries.
controllingFact: Paired queries across languages and revisions isolate language alignment from version mismatch.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Raise top-k until a reviewer can find the matching language passage.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Raising top-k can surface more candidates but does not diagnose whether language or revision alignment causes errors.

selectedOptionText: Reject any manifest built before the current deletion generation.
controllingFact: A build from generation 410 must not publish after deletion advances the active generation to 411.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Remove the source from the source store but leave the index active until the next scheduled rebuild.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A successful build says nothing about freshness relative to a later deletion.

selectedOptionText: Retrieve the antecedent with the sentence and preserve the section path.
controllingFact: Pronouns require the antecedent and section path to ground which plan the sentence governs.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Ask the model to resolve pronouns using its general knowledge of plan names.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: General model knowledge cannot establish the local antecedent or support the citation.

selectedOptionText: Replay role-specific queries against both headings and verify scope and citations.
controllingFact: Role-specific query replay checks whether the renamed heading changes retrieval scope and citations before full rebuild.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Compare only corpus-wide average similarity scores before and after the rename.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Corpus-wide average similarity can hide the affected role queries and scope errors.

selectedOptionText: Fetch the active revision and its changed exception table before answering.
controllingFact: The active revision 9 and changed exception table govern current policy; retrieve current linked evidence before answering.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Use revision 8 because it is a direct paragraph match and the body appears unchanged.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Revision 8 may match text but is superseded and misses the changed applicability exception.

selectedOptionText: Retrieve the appendix value with its applicability condition and source link.
controllingFact: The appendix value is valid only under the procedure’s date condition; retrieve and link both value and applicability.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Increase top-k so the procedure might appear somewhere among additional chunks.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: More top-k may return the condition but does not ensure the result binds it to the cited appendix value.

selectedOptionText: Retrieve the eligibility definition with the refund exception and retain both citations.
controllingFact: The generated summary conflicts with source text; answer from the authoritative eligibility/refund passages and cite both.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Use the generated summary because it was created from the source and is shorter.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: The summary is demonstrably lossy and omits the second-approver constraint.

selectedOptionText: Narrow by product and version, then expand to linked procedure evidence as needed.
controllingFact: Evaluation must cover both standalone warnings and warning applicability inside versioned linked workflows; no single frequency-only set suffices.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Use only frequent warning queries because they dominate production traffic.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Frequent warning-only cases miss the cross-section applicability question posed.

controllingFact: The failure concerns a cross-page eligibility definition and refund exception. None of the options repairs the evidence link while preserving source provenance; test linked retrieval of pages 3–4 with eligibility and exception citations.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Increase overlap until most page-3 text is duplicated on page 4, then keep citations at page level.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Increasing overlap is the closest retrieval repair, but page-level citations and arbitrary duplication still fail to guarantee the exact eligibility relationship.

controllingFact: The stem calls for product/version scoping plus selective expansion for multi-section procedures. None of the choices proposes that; the presented “correct” option is about summaries as locators, unrelated to the flat namespace.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Search all paragraphs globally, then rely on the model to discard other product versions from a large top-k.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Global search with large top-k is closest to finding procedures, but mixes versions and increases noise rather than testing a scoped hierarchy.

controllingFact: Current global revision with tenant-specific manifests points to tenant activation/manifest propagation. No option diagnoses that; the offered “correct” option is an unrelated warning/workflow retrieval test.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Rebuild the global index again because the global source revision is already current.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Rebuilding globally is a plausible first thought, but global revision is already current and does not reconcile differing tenant manifests.

selectedOptionText: Expose a governed MCP adapter for shared clients and keep the typed service backend.
controllingFact: A centrally managed, discoverable Claude connector can adapt the stable typed service while retaining its backend API boundary.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Replace the typed service API with a shell script copied into each client.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Copying a shell script to clients loses central rollout and schema discovery.

selectedOptionText: Keep bulk transfer on its streaming API and use MCP for bounded interactive inspection.
controllingFact: Bulk transfer needs resumability/checksums through the existing streaming data plane; MCP can serve bounded interactive inspection separately.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Send all eight million rows through MCP tool calls so both workloads use one protocol.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: MCP tool calls are a poor fit for moving millions of records and do not replace transfer checkpoints/backpressure.

selectedOptionText: Load compact capability metadata and fetch authorized record bodies on demand.
controllingFact: Load compact capability descriptions at session start and fetch authorized large bodies only on demand.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Return only record names forever and require users to open a separate system for every detail.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Names-only forever with external manual access fails the occasional in-client detail use case.

selectedOptionText: Retain the local CLI for offline scheduling; add a server only for a real shared consumer.
controllingFact: Offline cron has a stable local executable and no shared remote consumer or discovery need; local CLI is proportionate.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Introduce a remote MCP server so cron can negotiate a capability it already invokes locally.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A remote server introduces network negotiation to a task that must run offline.

selectedOptionText: Filter discovery by tenant and test both listings and execution authorization.
controllingFact: Tenant authorization must govern discovery metadata as well as invocation and resource reads.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Accept the design because actual calls and resource reads are denied across tenants.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Execution checks do not prevent leakage of other tenants’ tool names and resource titles.

selectedOptionText: Clarify whether the capability is a deterministic tool operation or an owned agent workflow, then assign orchestration and completion state to the appropriate layer.
controllingFact: Long-running delegated research needs owned orchestration and completion state; review workflow ownership before adding protocol calls.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Switch to an API for every worker call without changing workflow ownership.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Changing the per-worker transport does not establish who owns retries, partial completion, and synthesis.

selectedOptionText: Version the schema and verify compatibility across representative clients before rollout.
controllingFact: Version the schema and validate representative clients before rollout because clients currently interpret changes differently.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Deploy the schema change first and tell clients to retry if parsing fails.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Retrying after malformed parsing cannot make incompatible schema semantics safe.

selectedOptionText: Separate the owned research workflow from the tools its workers use.
controllingFact: The requested multi-agent research workflow owns orchestration/provenance; MCP tools can remain worker capabilities.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Keep the design and simply raise the token limit for the lead’s final prompt.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A larger prompt does not establish provenance or reliable structured merge across independent workers.

selectedOptionText: Use a narrow MCP adapter for shared Claude clients and retain the API boundary.
controllingFact: A narrow MCP adapter exposes discoverable operations to shared clients while retaining the secure API boundary.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Give every client a copy of the API credentials and a hand-written prompt describing the endpoint.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Duplicating credentials and handwritten endpoint instructions loses centralized control and expands credential distribution.

selectedOptionText: Keep bulk movement on the resumable, checksum-verified data plane.
controllingFact: Resumable, checksum-verified transfer belongs on the existing data plane; agent calls do not improve the required transport guarantees.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Use agent-to-agent delegation so multiple agents can upload separate fragments.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Delegation fragments orchestration but does not provide the established transfer/checksum semantics.

selectedOptionText: Refresh or renegotiate capabilities after the server’s enabled feature set changes.
controllingFact: In the pinned 2025-06-18 MCP tools spec, listChanged indicates the server will notify on tool-list changes; clients can then refresh tools/list. Because the scenario says the server emits no notification, verify/fix that server event path. Capability renegotiation is not the specified dynamic tool-list refresh mechanism.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Keep the startup list immutable until every client reconnects, even when the server already supports list-change notification.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: An immutable startup list until reconnect ignores the declared list-change notification contract and leaves the administrator-enabled tool unavailable to connected clients.

selectedOptionText: Enforce destination and resource authorization at the privileged server boundary.
controllingFact: The privileged server must authorize URI destination and resource access; client-side listing is not a trust boundary.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Trust the client to list only approved resources, then read any syntactically valid URI it submits.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A URI that parses can still escape the approved workspace.

selectedOptionText: Compare full-policy cost per resolution, including retries, failures, and latency.
controllingFact: Compare expected total policy cost per resolved case, including retry attempts/failures and relevant latency, rather than per-attempt price.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Compare only cost among successful first attempts.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: First-attempt cost ignores the retry policy that materially changes both resolution and spend.

selectedOptionText: Test cache placement against this slice’s p95 budget and quality floor.
controllingFact: The 120ms cache overhead exceeds the remaining 80ms p95 margin; test placement on this constrained slice while preserving quality.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Enable caching because lower spend outweighs a small latency increase.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Lower spend cannot make a route compliant when measured latency exceeds its remaining budget.

selectedOptionText: Constrain output to required fields and measure validity, tokens, and route p95.
controllingFact: Constrain structured output to required fields and measure schema validity, token use, and end-to-end p95.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Truncate responses after the five field names appear.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Truncating after field names risks incomplete values and invalid output.

selectedOptionText: Use query-aware bounded retrieval with a staged expansion when initial evidence is insufficient, then compare recall, p95, and 429 rate.
controllingFact: Query-aware bounded retrieval with evidence-triggered expansion addresses over-fetch while measuring recall, tail latency, and throttling.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Limit every request permanently to the top three sources without measuring recall.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A permanent top-three cap can silently lose evidence because recall is unmeasured.

selectedOptionText: Route premium work to a configuration that meets its slice-specific floor.
controllingFact: Premium traffic must meet its own 90% floor; route that slice to a qualifying configuration.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Adopt the candidate everywhere because routine volume dominates aggregate quality.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Aggregate routine quality cannot offset premium completeness falling below its explicit floor.

selectedOptionText: Evaluate caching by prefix reuse count, full lifecycle cost, and route latency.
controllingFact: Cache policy should account for write and read lifecycle cost, reuse frequency, quality, and route latency.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Compare cache-read token price alone with uncached token price.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Read-price-only comparisons omit the write cost and the one-time versus repeated-use distinction.

selectedOptionText: Decompose comparable slices by mix, retries, tokens, and cost per resolution.
controllingFact: Compare like task/mix slices, retries, tokens, and cost per resolution before attributing the increase to model pricing.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Compare total daily spend without normalizing request volume or task type.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Unnormalized daily totals confound traffic volume and task complexity.

selectedOptionText: Fix the argument contract and retry only plausibly transient failures.
controllingFact: Retries do not repair deterministic malformed arguments; fix the contract and retry only plausibly transient errors.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Increase retry count to recover more malformed calls.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: More attempts repeat a deterministic defect, inflate cost, and worsen the already-breached p95.

selectedOptionText: Evaluate cache impact against each slice’s latency and quality constraints.
controllingFact: The 250ms penalty fits the broad 300ms margin but exceeds the high-risk slice’s 100ms margin; evaluate constraints per slice.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Roll out globally because the aggregate p95 increase fits inside the route-wide margin.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Route-wide aggregate margin hides noncompliance for the constrained high-risk cohort.

selectedOptionText: Restore the evidence dependency before accepting the latency change.
controllingFact: Verification must wait for all evidence dependencies; otherwise 7% of results are generated without required evidence.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Accept because 93% of requests preserve the original ordering and average latency improved.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A 93% success rate and average latency do not justify violating the evidence ordering contract.

selectedOptionText: Route by the quality floor of each request class and measure each slice.
controllingFact: The urgent slice misses its explicit floor; keep it on a qualifying route and evaluate other classes independently.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Accept the route globally because the overall average score is unchanged and urgent cases are rare.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Routine majority cannot compensate for a failed critical-class quality constraint.

selectedOptionText: Use schema-aware output control and preserve the required completeness floor.
controllingFact: Six percent omissions imply 94% completeness, below the 99% floor; use schema-aware controls and preserve validity.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Keep the cap because the average response still contains most required fields and cost is on target.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Lower cost cannot offset a hard completeness-floor breach.

selectedOptionText: Compare total batch cost and quality under the budget, and verify that each route completes within the asynchronous deadline rather than applying an interactive p95 target.
controllingFact: This is a batch job with a 10-minute completion deadline and daily budget; compare full batch cost/quality and deadline compliance.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Choose A immediately because cost is the only hard constraint stated.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: An interactive 3-second p95 is not part of the stated batch contract.

selectedOptionText: Use application-side request records with stable ticket-to-operation links and reconcile their measured usage to provider aggregates at supported time and workspace scope.
controllingFact: Provider aggregate lacks ticket keys, so use stable app operation links for app-side measured usage and reconcile only at provider-supported grain.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Join each ticket to the nearest provider timestamp and call that exact attribution.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Nearest-time matching cannot establish exact ticket attribution with concurrent requests.

selectedOptionText: Mark route outcomes unknown, alert on exporter health, and keep edge traffic separate.
controllingFact: A stale exporter means missing application telemetry, not zero failures; surface unknown coverage/health and keep edge counts separate.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Keep zero failures because no error spans arrived.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: No error spans from a stale exporter are absence of evidence, not evidence of zero failures.

selectedOptionText: Join prompt/index versions to sampled groundedness outcomes and request metrics.
controllingFact: Groundedness regression needs prompt/index version and source IDs joined to outcomes; tokens alone do not explain grounding.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Treat higher cache reads as proof that the correct prompt was reused.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: More cache reads do not prove the correct prompt or retrieval evidence was used.

selectedOptionText: Trace opaque tenant binding through retrieval and validate it before delivery.
controllingFact: Opaque tenant-binding identifiers can expose cross-tenant filter reuse while minimizing customer content collection; validate before delivery.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Add more provider token charts because a wrong filter may change token totals.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Token charts are indirect and may remain normal despite returning another tenant’s data.

selectedOptionText: Remove the unsupported many-to-one attribution, report provider totals once at their actual scope, and show retry counts separately until a valid request-level mapping exists.
controllingFact: Provider totals are only valid at workspace/hour scope; avoid multiplying them across retry attempts and show retry counts separately pending valid mapping.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Keep the join and add a note that totals are approximate.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Dividing a duplicated aggregate by retry count fabricates exact per-attempt usage without a request-level key.

controllingFact: The needed view separates current delivery metrics from delayed reviewer quality labels and shows their freshness/coverage. No option does this; the keyed option instead describes cost-grain handling.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Ignore groundedness until labels are available in real time.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Ignoring quality loses the observed citation regression, while current completion cannot substitute for delayed groundedness labels.

selectedOptionText: Compare aggregate provider usage by its supported workspace/time/model dimensions with application retry counts by route/release, and label the comparison as correlated rather than request-exact.
controllingFact: Compare provider usage at its workspace/time/model grain with route/release retry counts, labeling the relation as correlation rather than exact attribution.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Conclude that retries caused the spend increase because both rose in the same hour.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: A same-hour co-movement does not prove retries caused the aggregate spend increase.

controllingFact: With an approved traffic increase, retain spend guardrails and normalize spend to workload using a reviewed baseline. None of the offered options states this; the marked choice is about delayed quality cohorts.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Raise the threshold until alerts stop without measuring the new workload baseline.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Raising a raw threshold without a workload baseline masks whether per-request economics actually worsened.

controllingFact: Cost per resolved case requires aligned usage and completion cohort windows/grain. None of these options addresses the one-day versus seven-day mismatch; the marked choice concerns attribution grain.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Scale the one-day spend to seven days using the latest daily average.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Scaling one day by an assumed average invents a comparable period without evidence.

selectedOptionText: Report the observed aggregate and leave route attribution unknown without a valid join.
controllingFact: Without route/task labels, the aggregate token increase is observable but route attribution is unknown; instrument a valid join before assigning cause.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Assume the model became more verbose because workspace output tokens increased.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Assuming model verbosity from workspace totals confounds workload mix and lacks request-level evidence.

controllingFact: Separate provider transport success from client parsing and application-complete structured output; HTTP 200 and tokens are insufficient. None of the options says this; the marked option is unrelated ingestion deduplication.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: HTTP status and total tokens only.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: HTTP status and token count still mark the failed parse as success.

selectedOptionText: Separate provider-attempt usage from end-to-end request cost and resolution.
controllingFact: Provider spend is measured at workspace/model grain while route telemetry is finer and shared; report provider attempt usage separately from route/request resolution.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Split the aggregate evenly between the two routes and use that as measured route spend.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Evenly splitting a shared aggregate between routes invents route-level spend.

controllingFact: Overlapping usage windows require stable-record deduplication or atomic replacement of the overlap before aggregation; none of the options implements this.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Increase the polling interval so overlapping windows are less likely, without changing ingestion semantics.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Increasing polling intervals may reduce overlap frequency but leaves ingestion incorrect when retries overlap.

controllingFact: The route metric must include cache-served outcomes and account for cache costs while separating provider usage for provider-called requests; no offered option captures these dimensions coherently.

nearestCredibleCompetitor.text: Count each cached response as zero-cost and report provider tokens per completed application span.
nearestCredibleCompetitor.whyItFails: Treating cache hits as zero-cost ignores cache/write/storage costs and provider tokens per application span does not measure full cost per successful case.
